summary: Submitted sourced research feedback closing another unread peripheral area, the network transport's RPC admission and heartbeat fast-path, with three new SourceRanges (S-net-transport-command, net_transport.go:639-742; S-raft-process-heartbeat, raft.go:1415-1437; S-raft-heartbeat-fastpath, api.go:613-616). The answer records that the fast path is safe as documented and that admission adds no separate obligation: the transport decodes each command with a bounded InstallSnapshot reader, and it classifies an AppendEntries as a heartbeat only under a strict conjunction (non-zero term, leader address present, PrevLogEntry and PrevLogTerm zero, no entries, LeaderCommitIndex zero), so any entry- or commit-carrying AppendEntries always goes to the main consumer. For an entry-less heartbeat the handler reached can only call setState/setCurrentTerm (atomic stores), setLeader (leader lock), skip the previous-log and entries blocks and the commit update, and set last contact under its lock while reading the cached last index under the state lock - no plain configurations field write and no LogStore call - which is what makes the documented concurrent-call requirement hold. Remaining work is listed explicitly: tcp_transport and pooling, the FSM batch manager, NewRaft startup reconstruction, testing helpers, and the Raft.Restore reporting ambiguity recorded earlier. No map change is proposed because nothing contradicts an accepted object. Preflight returned valid:true; the run's five confirmed_in_scope conclusions across six implementation_reproduced findings are unchanged.
